title: Gradekeeper: Dynamic golden-prompt weighting + cohort holdback orchestrator for staged rollouts
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Implement 'Gradekeeper', a lightweight orchestrator that: (1) continuously re-weights a project's golden prompt set by signal freshness and discriminatory power, (2) applies cohort-aware holdbacks for A/B and canary traffic based on those weights, and (3) triggers automated quarantine/rollback actions with configurable hysteresis. The goal is to reduce false positives from stale golden prompts and provide a more targeted rollback mechanism when regressions are concentrated in specific cohorts.
background: Current golden-set gating treats all prompts as equal and often overreacts to noise from low-signal prompts or rare cohorts. On several rollouts we've seen spurious aborts caused by prompts that had low coverage and high variance. We need a system that (a) scores golden prompts by usefulness, (b) surfaces cohort-specific regressions, and (c) integrates with the existing rollout conductor to perform safe, reversible actions.
proposed_solution: Build Gradekeeper as three cooperating pieces: 1) Weighted Golden Service - maintains per-prompt metadata (coverage, variance, AUC/discrimination) and produces a rolling weight vector; 2) Cohort Sampler - maps incoming traffic to cohorts (tenant, locale, intent cluster) and computes cohort-level score deltas against the weighted golden baseline; 3) Quarantine Orchestrator - policies to isolate a cohort, reduce traffic weight, or auto-rollback only when weighted, cohorted regression signals exceed thresholds with hysteresis and manual override gates.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Shadow-mode for 4 weeks on low-risk tenants to calibrate prompt weights and cohort mapping. Phase 2: Soft canary - enable active gating for 5% traffic with automated alerts but no auto-rollback. Phase 3: Enable quarantine actions and auto-rollback with conservative thresholds and human-in-loop approval for P0 regressions.
monitoring_plan: Expose per-prompt weight drift graphs, cohort delta heatmaps, and a single quality-index (weighted-score-drop) per rollout. Create two dashboards: gradekeeper/overview and gradekeeper/cohort-details. Integrate Slack + Opsgenie alerts for (a) sudden global weighted-score drops, (b) cohort-specific persistent drops exceeding hysteresis window, (c) quarantine toggles executed.
acceptance_criteria: Weighted golden service runs at <200ms median latency for weight refresh path
Cohort sampler correctly assigns >95% synthetic samples to expected cohort labels (unit tests)
Shadow-mode produces weight vectors and cohort deltas for at least 3 real releases without false auto-quarantine actions
Dashboards show both prompt-level and cohort-level regressions and are queryable by rollout id
Auto-quarantine/rollback can be toggled per-customer and per-release from Console and respects canary weight fractions

comments: PM (Rafael Ortiz): We need to ensure this is explainable to SREs — include 'why' for every quarantine event (top contributing prompts/cohorts).
Design (Monica Lee): Dashboard prototypes look good; add a compact alert summary for on-call flow so we don't force engineers into the full console during incidents.
Eng Review (Priya Shah): Consider adding a decay factor for prompt weights to handle sudden shifts (e.g., new product feature causing prompt distribution shift).
SRE (Liam O'Connor): Suggest default hysteresis of 3 measurement windows before auto-quarantine; we can tune after shadow run.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting weights to a small historical eval set -> Mitigation: require minimum coverage threshold and cross-validate weights on recent shadowed traffic.
Risk: Frequent quarantines on noisy cohorts -> Mitigation: enforce hysteresis and a minimum absolute traffic threshold before any action.
Risk: Increased CPU for weight computation -> Mitigation: batch weight refreshes off the hot path and cache frequent results for 1 minute.
Risk: False sense of safety -> Mitigation: ensure manual rollback path remains simple and documented; include runbook links in dashboards.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on: (1) the proposed weight decay math and failure modes, (2) the quarantine policy edge cases (mixed cohort signals), (3) Console UX for per-customer toggles. Also validate that the shadow metrics are instrumented using the standard rollout telemetry schema.
